runs.text: An AI teammate for ongoing work

Today we will choose between three ways of working with AI. Dot is useful when you want follow-through over time. A repeated check and a focused task are different needs. This presentation uses the built-in Claude Code command; a custom loop may behave differently.
It keeps work moving between conversations.
Its own cloud computer can work while your laptop is off.

Think of an assistant who remembers the assignment and follows up between conversations. Dot can research, work with documents and data, and help build software. It can finish an individual task even while a broader responsibility continues. Availability is rolling out and depends on account and workspace access.
Tries a fix, runs a test,
“Has a test” versus “uses judgment” does not separate Dot from /loop.

The original verifier idea describes a custom repair loop: attempt, test, fix, repeat. It is useful, but it is not the definition of Claude Code’s built-in /loop. In current Claude Code, omitting an interval can let Claude choose the delay. Both approaches involve model judgment. Dot can use objective checks too.

A clear finish line? A normal task—or Codex Goal—may be enough.

These are recommended defaults, not exclusive capabilities. A normal Codex task can investigate, edit and test within one request. Dot adds coordination and follow-up across work. For a difficult task with a measurable finish line, Codex Goals are another option.
“Fix the broken signup button and test it.”
“Check the release build every five minutes.”
“Track launch blockers this week. Prepare updates
and bring me decisions that need my input.”

Illustrative examples, assuming the needed tools are connected. The distinction is what you are delegating: a deliverable, a repeated check, or responsibility for follow-through. Dot could coordinate a code fix, but opening Codex directly is usually simpler when that fix is all you need.
Use the desktop sidebar or ChatGPT on a desktop browser.
Add the apps and files needed for this responsibility.
Name the result, timing, updates, and decisions you keep.
Correct missing context before adding more work.

In the desktop app, open the Your dot area if shown; official documentation describes setup in ChatGPT desktop or a desktop browser. Follow the introduction. Account availability varies. Computer access is optional, and messaging access does not automatically connect files or apps.
Keep our product demo ready for Friday.
Use the demo checklist and connected project channel.
Check each weekday at 9 AM Asia/Tehran until Friday.
Update the checklist when a deadline or owner changes.
Tell me here only if the demo is at risk or you need a decision.
Draft team messages for my review. Confirm the schedule.
Result + sources + timing + notification rule + approval boundary

This is an illustrative team prompt. Replace the sources with material your dot can access. After it replies, check the saved schedule and inspect the first checklist. Refine what counts as a blocker using feedback. This does not mean the underlying model is retrained.
Use Codex directly for a focused edit, bug fix, or review.
Use Dot when you want follow-up across tasks and time.
Keep it online with the app open.
Set up a Codex cloud environment
Long task, clear end point? Use a Codex Goal with evidence of success.

Dot can create and coordinate tasks, including coding tasks. New cloud coding work needs a configured Codex cloud environment. Existing tasks stay on their original environment. A delegated task has its own conversation; it does not automatically inherit every Dot conversation.
Review, steer, and stop the work
Stop delegated tasks and schedules separately.

Built-in review and app permissions apply. The same rules can permit an action, ask for approval, or require a step from you. A completion message is not proof that an output is correct: inspect it. Stopping work does not reverse completed changes.
Try it: “Keep next week’s client demo on track.”

Ask the room to choose: “Summarize this document” → normal chat. “Check the build while I work” → /loop. “Keep next week’s client demo on track” → Dot. These recommendations are based on scope and follow-up, not whether a result is subjective. For fixed-interval /loop, ask Claude to cancel the job when finished; recurring jobs expire after seven days in current docs. Re-check product documentation before reusing this deck after feature changes.
